## 1 · Goals
Weekdays 08:30. Two numbers and one focus, read off the person's row — not written by the model. The date key is minted here; tonight's reply rebuilds it and updates the same row instead of appending a second one.

## 2 · Check-in
The regex owns the log. "6", "6/3" and "none" are read here and written straight to the sheet — no model touches the number on a normal evening. Everything else is handed to the coach in lane 3.

'' : ', ' + $('Did the regex read it?').item.json.hours + 'h of ' + $('Did the regex read it?').item.json.hours_cap + 'h' }}. {{ Number($('Did the regex read it?').item.json.calls) >= Number($('Did the regex read it?').item.json.calls_target) ? 'Target hit.' : (Number($('Did the regex read it?').item.json.calls_target) - Number($('Did the regex read it?').item.json.calls)) + ' short.' }}

parameters.content:
## 3 · Coach
One agent for everyone on the list. It logs what the person actually said and coaches from the Notion playbook library — and from nothing else. It cannot set a goal, move a target or quote a number that is not in a playbook row. If Anthropic is down the person is asked for a plain number instead, which lane 2 can still log.

options.systemMessage:
You are a coach, messaging one of the people you work with on WhatsApp. You have two jobs.

1. Log the day. If the message says how many calls they held or how many hours they spent, call log_the_day with exactly those numbers. Never guess one they did not give — leave it out. Say what you logged.

2. Coach. Use read_the_playbooks to find tasks whose Focus matches theirs, and name at most one, with the playbook it comes from. Coach on behaviour, cadence and what to stop doing.

Hard limits. Never state a price, a policy, a target or a number that is not in the prompt or in a playbook row you just read. If they ask for one you do not have, say you do not have it and tell them to raise it with whoever set their goals. Never set or change a goal yourself.

You coach several people. Nothing one person tells you may appear in a reply to anyone else.

Reply in at most 60 words. No emoji, no greeting, no sign-off, no links, no bullet lists — plain sentences someone reads on a phone.

parameters.toolDescription: Write this person's numbers for today into the log. Call this only when the message actually states how many calls they held, or how many hours they spent on them.

value.name: ={{ $json.name }}
value.calls: ={{ $fromAI('calls', 'How many calls the person says they held today. Omit if they did not say.', 'number') }}
value.hours: ={{ $fromAI('hours', 'How many hours the person says they spent on calls today. Omit if they did not say.', 'number') }}
value.note: ={{ $fromAI('note', 'Why, in at most six words, for example "two no-shows" or "delivery fire". Empty if they gave no reason.', 'string') }}

parameters.toolDescription: Read the playbook library: every task, the Focus it belongs to, its pillar, its priority, the playbook it comes from and how long it takes. Takes no arguments. Ignore any row whose Active is false — those tasks are retired.

assignments.name: message
assignments.value: ={{ ($json.output || '').trim().replace(/^["']|["']$/g, '').slice(0, 900) || "I couldn't read a number out of that. How many calls did you hold today? Just the number is fine." }}

parameters.content:
## Known defects
**The coach forgets everyone within the hour.** `Remember the thread` is n8n's Simple Memory: a Map held in the n8n process, swept on every read, dropping any thread not touched for 60 minutes. A daily check-in is the worst case for it — someone answers the 08:30 message at 17:00 and the coach has no memory of the morning. It is also process-local, so a restart clears it and queue-mode workers each keep their own copy of a different half of the conversation.

`contextWindowLength: 6` bounds **turns, not tokens**, so one pasted wall of text still goes to the model whole.

**Fix:** a persistent chat memory (Postgres or Redis), or drop the memory node and read the last few `Days` rows into the prompt — the sheet already holds the history, deterministically and for free.

## TODO
Not built, deliberately — this canvas is the daily loop only.

- **Weekly scoring.** Each focus against its target, in a Code node so the scoring stays deterministic.
- **One focus at a time.** When several things are off target, name one and queue the rest.
- **Friday scorecard.** The week as a chart, to the person and to whoever coaches them.
- **Chase the quiet.** A nudge for anyone who never replied, respecting the WhatsApp 24-hour window.
- **Call them, don't only text (ElevenLabs).** A ringing phone is a different kind of interrupt from a message that sits unread all evening. An ElevenLabs voice agent could place the nudge as an outbound call and take the number by voice. It also sidesteps the WhatsApp 24-hour window, which governs WhatsApp messages and not calls — at the cost of needing explicit consent to ring someone, which the `People` sheet would have to record and honour.
- **Evals.** Groundedness and logging accuracy on the coach reply, before any of the above.
